clue.text: Different people — not her sort, not all of them

indicators.note: only part of the letters of these three words is used, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a group as unlike her and her kind, conceding a few exceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not her sort' reads as a snobbish remark; 'not all of them' says the answer sits inside those words, running from the O of 'not' into 'sort'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest, the remaining people apart from oneself, are those who are different.

clue.text: City offering what's collected in box for down-and-outs

indicators.note: the letters gathered inside these words make the answer

explanation.surface: A city offers money put in a charity tin for the homeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's collected in' sounds like donations in a charity box, but it signals the answer within 'box for down'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English university city, an example of a city.

clue.text: Protests on the go when food is not available

parts.note: hunger is what is felt when there is no food
marches means is on the move, is on the go

explanation.surface: Demonstrators keep walking though they have nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunger marches were protest walks by the unemployed, famously the 1930s Jarrow March in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: These were processions in protest at unemployment and poverty, a kind of demonstration.

clue.text: One book is missing from new libraries, they protest

indicators.note: a new form of letters is a fresh arrangement
the one and the book are absent from the word libraries

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Reading rooms short of a volume draw complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is missing' takes I and B from LIBRARIES, leaving LRARIES; 'new' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rail complain loudly and bitterly, so they are protesters.

clue.text: Calm little place, attended by a group of detectives

parts.note: Pl. is the short form of place, as in street names
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A sleepy village is visited by a squad of police investigators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little place' is the abbreviation PL, as in addresses. CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone placid is serene and untroubled.

clue.text: Fall in part of race, starts to seem exhausted

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a race

indicators.note: the beginnings of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A runner stumbles during one circuit, looking worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lapse is a slip or decline, as in a fall from standards.

clue.text: Groups of stars interfered with colonial's tent

indicators.note: letters interfered with are disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: Someone tampered with a settler's shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers name recognised patterns of stars such as Orion; each is one of these.

clue.text: Proper journey down mountain maybe without first sign of snow

indicators.note: the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a descent is a journey downward, a mountain one being an example

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A sensible climber comes down before the snow arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes S, the 'first sign of snow', from DESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: decent behaviour is respectable and seemly.

clue.text: Proverbial drinker outside pub is European

indicators.note: the drinker stands around the pub, so its letters go on both sides

parts.note: the saying 'to drink like a fish' makes the fish the proverbial drinker
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A legendary boozer standing outside a bar turns out to be from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the drinker around the pub; 'to drink like a fish' is the proverb behind the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Finland is a Finn, a nationality within Europe.

clue.text: Hard work is followed by whisky and a game

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come first and the drink after them

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils
op is short for opus, a work
Scotch is whisky made in Scotland

explanation.surface: Hard labour, then a whisky and something to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Criticise one Conservative creating alarm

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Attacking a Tory politician causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sudden fear or fright.

clue.text: Female bird always returning full of energy

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the energy symbol within it
returning means the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A bird keeps coming back, brimming with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns EVER into REVE, and 'full of' puts E inside it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the ruff, a wading bird, is called a reeve.

clue.text: Northern city quickly attracting any number

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for a quick tempo
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A city in the North rapidly draws in crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston is a city in Lancashire in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Lancashire city, an example of a place in the north of England.

clue.text: Chum is dancing in front of everyone in entertainment venue

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new order

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A friend dances before the whole crowd at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles 'Chum is' into MUSICH; 'in front of' sets that before the word for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre for variety acts, popular in Victorian Britain, is an example of a place of entertainment.

clue.text: 'Innocent' Alice being false — no good inside

indicators.note: the two letters for no good go within the jumbled name
a false version of the name is a distorted rearrangement of it

explanation.surface: Alice's supposed innocence is a sham, with nothing good about her inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being false' scrambles the name to AELIC, and 'inside' sets the no-good abbreviation after its first letter. 'Innocent' in quotes hints it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: like an angel, pure and blameless.

clue.text: Grate fragment ending in fire

parts.note: a scrap is a fragment

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A shard left in the fireplace grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grate' looks like a fireplace noun but is the verb: to rub harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, both mean rubbing roughly against a surface with a harsh noise.

clue.text: My, my! It's a horse

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise like my
again, gee as an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at the sight of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee is British nursery talk for a horse, from the call 'gee up'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a childish or informal word for a horse, especially a racehorse.

clue.text: Small crown, gold one seen in court

indicators.note: the gold and one appear within the court abbreviation

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A little gold crown is spotted at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' places the heraldic gold and 'one' within the court abbreviation; 'court' misleads toward royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a lesser crown worn by nobles below the monarch.

clue.text: Girl in New York who looks after children?

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed within the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman in Manhattan wonders who minds the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is employed to care for a family's children.

clue.text: We hear horses eat in field

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, giving another spelt differently

parts.note: greys are grey horses

explanation.surface: Apparently the horses are feeding out in the pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: GREYS, grey horses, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals feeding on growing grass in a pasture are doing this.

clue.text: Like female not looking very well

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A woman appears to be poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pale and grey-faced, as from shock or illness.

clue.text: Stopping almost all night after travel

indicators.note: letters that have travelled have moved to new places, a rearrangement
almost the whole word means its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A traveller pulls up after journeying nearly through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of 'all', leaving AL; 'after travel' scrambles that with 'night'. 'travel' looks like a journey, but signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coming to a stop, or hesitant and faltering.

clue.text: Tries to present pieces for university tutor?

definitions.meaning: written compositions handed in to an academic supervisor

explanation.surface: A student makes attempts at producing work for a tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: an attempt is an assay, and students write short compositions for tutorials.

clue.text: Candlestick boy carried around cold Anglican church

indicators.note: the boy holds the cold letter, his letters on either side of it

parts.note: a son is a boy
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A boy carries a candle holder around a chilly parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried around' makes the boy enclose the cold letter, giving SCON; the Church of England abbreviation follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a candle holder, often fixed to a wall.
